Use case: illustration-story.
Medieval Georgian-Persian illuminated manuscript miniature painting illustrating Episode 13 of Shota Rustaveli's "The Knight in the Panther's Skin" (ვეფხისტყაოსანი): Avtandil's Return to Arabia & Sograt's Petition to Rostevan.
Setting: Arabia, a secluded terrace in Tinatin’s palace with a moonlit garden beyond.
Scene: Returned from his first quest, Avtandil kneels respectfully before Tinatin and recounts the discovery of Tariel. Tinatin leans toward him with attentive recognition, and his travel cloak and sword rest beside the steps. Only these TWO people appear, in a private nocturnal reunion rather than a public council. Avtandil kneels on one knee near the shallow steps of Tinatin's low royal seat, one hand over his heart and the other open in a storyteller's gesture. Tinatin listens intently, leaning slightly forward with tenderness and recognition. Use a starry lapis night sky, a crescent moon, softly lit carved arches, a fountain, cypresses and pomegranate leaves. Keep a restrained emotional warmth, not a wedding or coronation. His plain travel cloak and silver conical helmet rest on a step; a sheathed sword at his belt suggests the completed journey. No letter, paper, scroll or book is needed.
Characters: Avtandil matches reference 2: a youthful olive-skinned, clean-shaven man with wavy dark brown hair, expressive dark brows and brown eyes, silver-and-bronze mail/lamellar armor under a worn vermilion travel cloak and gold embroidered collar. Tinatin matches reference 3: a young olive-skinned queen with long wavy black hair, brown eyes and strong dark eyebrows, a jeweled antique-gold crown with a central ruby and blue gems, purple-and-gold brocade royal gown and ruby earrings. Her face and crown must differ clearly from Nestan's black veil/emerald costume.
Story constraints: Sograt’s petition to Rostevan occurs in a different audience; do not merge it into this lovers’ reunion. No written report, scroll or map is necessary. Do not show Rostevan, Sograt or Shermadin in this intimate scene.
Reference 1 is STYLE ONLY, not its poet, book or daytime composition. References 2 and 3 are IDENTITY ONLY for Avtandil and Tinatin; ignore circular portrait frames. Render a single coherent manuscript miniature scene, not separate panels or medallions.
Medieval Georgian-Persian illuminated manuscript miniature painting for Shota Rustaveli's "The Knight in the Panther's Skin" (ვეფხისტყაოსანი). 16th–17th-century Georgian royal manuscript miniature, Mamuka Tavakarashvili / King Vakhtang VI illumination tradition blended with classical Persian-Safavid tempera miniature. Egg tempera, lapis lazuli, malachite green, vermilion, warm ochre and burnished antique gold leaf on aged ivory-parchment vellum. Stylized faceted rocky cliffs, ornamental cypress and pomegranate trees, intricately patterned arches and domes, expressive courtly figures in medieval Georgian-Eastern attire. Fine controlled contours, delicately patterned fabrics, luminous matte mineral pigments, slightly flattened layered miniature space with expressive narrative gestures. A painted manuscript scene, not photorealism, cinematic rendering, modern digital fantasy or a collage of circular portraits. Reuse referenced character faces and coloring but adapt costume to the actual chronological story scene; Tariel wears ordinary Indian court or military attire in early backstory, his panther skin belongs to his later exile. Exact horizontal 16:10 composition, preferably native 1600x1000 pixels, a single coherent scene framed for a card vignette. Soft natural painted vignette dissolving to warm aged ivory vellum at edges, modest antique-gold floral flourishes at the perimeter, no rigid border. Key faces and gestures comfortably inside the central safe area, no important content cut off. STRICTLY NO TEXT, NO LETTERS, NO CAPTIONS, NO NUMBERS, NO INSCRIPTIONS, NO CALLIGRAPHY, NO BANNERS, NO SCROLLS, NO SIGNATURES, NO WATERMARKS anywhere. Architectural ornament must be purely floral/geometric with no pseudo-writing. If letters are narratively necessary, use a small closed plain unmarked folded paper or sealed envelope, never visible writing or rolled scrolls. All book covers/pages must be plain and unmarked. Do not show graphic blood or gore; imply violent events through gestures, context and intact clothing.
Mandatory horizontal16:10 painting, ideally native1600x1000. No text, lettering, numbers, banners or scrolls anywhere.
